I’ve attended a few classical music concerts before, and one of the basic rules is that audience members should not leave or enter their seats while a piece is being performed. It’s a matter of respect for both the performers’ concentration and the audience’s experience.

Honestly, I’ve had better concert etiquette experiences at K-pop concerts, where I would argue that the audience is not necessarily made up of people from the same economic demographic as Andrea Bocelli’s audience.

And what did the ushers do about it? ZERO. Was there any effort to ask these people to return to their seats? NONE. In fact, there wasn’t even an usher stationed in the audience area when the concert started.

Overall, I enjoyed the performance, but I did NOT enjoy the concert experience.
Shame on the audience members who showed absolutely no consideration for others, and shame on the staff who failed to do their jobs.
Yet throughout this concert, even the staff kept walking back and forth in the Gold section. How is that acceptable? It was incredibly distracting.
